title: AN5946 STM32N6 low-power modes

first_page_excerpt: Introduction This application note deals with the use of low-power modes on the STM32N6 devices. It is applicable to all the devices of the STM32N6 series. The STM32N6 devices are based on an Arm® Cortex®-M55 CPU using 16 nm FinFET technology. It can run up to 800 MHz (overdrive mode). The STM32N6 devices embed the Neural-ART accelerator, an NPU with its subsystems, which is designed to accelerate deep learning inference for AI applications. The NPU can run up to 1 GHz. They have an internal SMPS. With their built-in internal voltage regulator and voltage scaling, the consumption in active modes is kept at a minimum. The multivoltage domains of the device permit the core to be energized at a low voltage of 0.8 V, while the I/Os and analog components can function at a higher supply voltage of 1.8 V or 3.3 V. They support a backup domain, which can be supplied by a battery to keep the RTC running. The backup domain encompasses a collection of 32 registers, each of which is 32 bits wide, as well as 8 Kbytes of backup SRAM that can be accessed in 32-, 16-, or 8-bit data mode. This SRAM can be retained even in the event that the MCU experiences a loss of the primary power supply. The backup battery can be charged when the main supply is plugged in. The STM32N6 devices have low-power capabilities to reduce the power consumption. They support different low-power modes that can achieve the best compromise between low-power consumption, shorter startup/wake-up time, and the number of active peripherals.
